section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the crown drawn on Shavuos is the true crown above Gulgalta, and that the two crowns corresponding to Naaseh and Nishma were bound through the precedence of Naaseh, elevating the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of mitzvos to the level of self-nullification to the Owner of the Will.
section.t: And behold, that which on the holiday of Shavuos is the drawing down of the crown,
it is the true crown that is above Gulgalta.
And similarly, regarding the two crowns corresponding to Naaseh and Nishma that were drawn on the eve of Shavuos,
they are encompassing lights that are above any relation to the internal.
And based on this, we can explain that the binding of the crown corresponding to Nishma was specifically through their having preceded Naaseh to Nishma,
because the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of mitzvos is a self-nullification to the will,
and since the mitzvos are commands to the person,
behold, the will of mitzvos is in the manner of the will
(of the person)
who wants to act through his powers,
[this is] the encompassing light of Gulgalta.
And the drawing down of the encompassing light of the crown
(an encompassing light that is above any relation to the internal)
is through the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven,
self-nullification to the Owner of the will.
And by their having preceded Naaseh to Nishma,
they bound for themselves two crowns, one corresponding to Naaseh and one corresponding to Nishma,
because through the precedence of Naaseh to Nishma,
even the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of mitzvos is in a manner that there is felt within it in revelation
that it comes from the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven,
self-nullification to the Owner of the will.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the elevation in the self-nullification of Nishma through the precedence of Naaseh, showing that the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of mitzvos is to the revealed will, while the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of heaven is to the person's very existence as a servant of the King, and when Nishma follows Naaseh, the self-nullification of Nishma becomes total.
section.t: And the explanation of the elevation that occurs in the self-nullification of Nishma through the precedence of the self-nullification of Naaseh,
will be understood by first prefacing,
that just as Above,
the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of mitzvos is to the will
(revelation)
and the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven is to the Owner of the will,
so too is it regarding the person,
that the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of mitzvos is in the revelations of the person,
that he will do all that he is commanded, and moreover that this
(doing what he is commanded)
will be his will,
and the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven is in the person himself,
that his entire existence is that he is a servant of the King,
the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
And from this it is understood,
that the superiority of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven over accepting the yoke of mitzvos is also in the matter of self-nullification.
For in accepting the yoke of mitzvos,
there remains with him and in him an existence that is not nullified,
and the true self-nullification is in accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven,
that his entire existence is that he is a servant of the King.
[And this is that there must be
(also)
accepting the yoke of mitzvos, in order that the self-nullification be
(also)
regarding the actual fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos].
And when the self-nullification of Nishma
(accepting the yoke of mitzvos)
is after and through the precedence of the self-nullification of Naaseh
(accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven),
such that it is felt in revelation that this one who accepts upon himself to do all that he is commanded is because he himself is a servant of the King,
then,
even the self-nullification of Nishma is in his entire existence
(regarding his revealed powers),
and it is not at all possible that he will not fulfill the command.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section adds that just as in ratzo vashov the ultimate purpose of ratzo is for the subsequent shov, so too Naaseh (accepting the yoke of heaven) is the preface for Nishma (accepting the yoke of mitzvos), and through this precedence, an elevation is added to Naaseh itself, fulfilling the ultimate purpose of creating a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos.
section.t: And we may add,
that just as in ratzo vashov,
the ultimate intention of the ratzo is for the sake of the shov that comes after the ratzo,
so too is it with Naaseh
(accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven)
and Nishma
(accepting the yoke of mitzvos)
which are like ratzo vashov,
that the ultimate intention of Naaseh is that it bring about Nishma.
And through the precedence of Naaseh to Nishma,
that Naaseh is a preface to Nishma,
an elevation is added in Naaseh.
For the self-nullification of Naaseh
(in and of itself),
although it is a self-nullification of mesirus nefesh which is the most elevated self-nullification,
it is the self-nullification of the person,
and by Naaseh being a preface to Nishma, to accept upon himself the yoke of mitzvos
(shov and drawing down below),
through this the intention is completed that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place in the lower realms,
the intention of the Awtsmoos.
And we may add,
that the superiority of Nishma that comes through the precedence of Naaseh over the matter of Naaseh itself is also in the self-nullification.
For the self-nullification of Naaseh
(in and of itself)
is that he is not an existence unto himself
(and he is only a servant of the King),
and through the precedence of Naaseh to Nishma,
[such] that the self-nullification of Nishma is analogous to the self-nullification of Naaseh,
the self-nullification is also in the very existence of the person.
